items.headline: Trump lands in Manila to open Asia trip
items.summary: President Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday, the first stop of a three-day trip focused on economic deals. The trip ends in China with rare three-way nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

items.headline: U.S. closes remote-access loophole on AI chips
items.summary: The Trump administration issued rules restricting remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, closing a gap that let Chinese companies use them despite limits on physical sales. The move comes ahead of Trump's meeting with Xi amid the Nvidia fallout.

items.headline: Third U.S. aircraft carrier reaches Middle East
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, giving the U.S. three carriers in the region, a U.S. official confirmed Monday. President Trump is keeping his options open in the Iran war.

items.headline: White House requires approval before officials testify
items.summary: White House counsel Will Scharf issued a memo directing federal agencies to get approval from the White House legal and legislative affairs offices before agreeing to testify before Congress. The memo applies across the executive branch.

items.headline: Outages hit major banks and United Airlines
items.summary: Customers at several major U.S. banks had trouble reaching their accounts Monday after JPMorgan Chase disclosed a technical issue it said was not cyber-related. United Airlines separately resolved a technology problem that delayed departing flights.

items.headline: Ground stop sparks FAA funding fight in Congress
items.summary: Lawmakers are debating FAA funding and air traffic control upgrades after a communications failure caused last week's nationwide ground stop. The dispute follows Trump's demand for more money beyond the $12.5 billion Congress recently approved.

items.headline: Russia claims record drone downings; Kyiv hits Crimea bridge
items.summary: Russia said it intercepted more than 1,300 Ukrainian drones, its largest claimed total of the war, as Ukraine struck a key bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a second day. EU countries accused Moscow of stalling peace talks while bombing power plants ahead of winter.

items.headline: Fossil-fuel phaseout coalition presses on at COP31
items.summary: A coalition seeking a faster move away from fossil fuels is unveiling new national plans at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. It is going ahead despite the withdrawal of Colombia, its original champion.

items.headline: California sues OpenAI over hacking incident
items.summary: California's attorney general sued OpenAI, arguing that the Hugging Face hacking attack was foreseeable because of the company's security practices. The suit focuses on the risks posed by the company's handling of security.

items.headline: Two mass shootings kill at least 17 in South Africa
items.summary: At least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on the same day about 530 kilometers apart in South Africa. Police said the motives had not yet been established.

digest.overview:
President Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday to open a three-day Asia trip that ends in China with rare three-way nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Ahead of the summit, the administration issued rules closing a loophole that let Chinese firms remotely use advanced U.S. AI chips, and Trump backed a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive. The USS Theodore Roosevelt became the third U.S. aircraft carrier in the Middle East as Trump keeps his options open in the Iran war. A new White House memo requires agency officials to get approval before testifying to Congress. Lawmakers clashed over FAA funding after last week's nationwide ground stop, while customers of JPMorgan Chase and other big banks lost online access Monday and United Airlines fixed a glitch that delayed departures. California sued OpenAI over a hacking incident it called foreseeable, and Raye and Rosalía lead the 2027 Grammy nominations.

Abroad, Russia said it shot down more than 1,300 Ukrainian drones in one attack, its highest claimed total of the war, as Kyiv struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a second day. EU governments accused Moscow of dragging out peace talks while bombing power plants before winter. Countries meeting in Geneva negotiated limits on autonomous weapons, with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting binding rules. At least 17 people died in two mass shootings in South Africa. At the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, a coalition pushing to move away from fossil fuels unveiled new national plans despite Colombia's exit.

home.overview:
The Chargers finally won, beating Baltimore 23–20 on Monday night as Omarion Hampton ran for 105 yards and Justin Herbert scored on a 22-yard run, sending the Ravens to 4–6 and a fifth straight loss. New England fears Drake Maye fractured his ankle in Munich, and Week 11 opens Thursday with the Colts at Houston. In the NBA, Orlando won 115–105 in Boston, Joel Embiid's 37 points lifted Philadelphia to 12–3 and the East's best record, Donovan Mitchell scored 39 for Cleveland, and Phoenix won in Denver despite Nikola Jokic's 28 and 15. Tuesday brings Pistons-Spurs and Knicks-Raptors, and baseball's qualifying-offer deadline hits at 4 p.m. ET.

Germany routed the Netherlands 5–0 in Berlin, with Florian Wirtz scoring twice, to win their Nations League group, and both teams are through to the quarterfinals ahead of Friday's draw. Tonight Wales host Portugal, Denmark meet Norway, South Korea close their year in Qatar, and the USA face Haiti in Mauricio Pochettino's farewell before he starts at Manchester United. The Premier League, La Liga and K League return this weekend, with Suwon Samsung one point from the K League 2 title. In the KBO, free agency opens today, with Korean Series MVP Koo Ja-wook eyeing the majors.

fact.question: Why do onions make you cry?
fact.answer:
When you cut an onion, you break open its cells and release an enzyme called lachrymatory-factor synthase. It turns the onion's sulfur compounds (via sulfenic acid) into a gas, syn-propanethial-S-oxide.

That gas drifts up to your eyes and irritates them, and your tear glands respond by flushing it away. Scientists only identified this enzyme in 2002; before that, a different enzyme, alliinase, was thought to be the cause.

The practical fix: refrigerate or freeze the onion before chopping, which slows the reaction, or choose sweet onions, which carry less sulfur.
